assessment.summary: A present, quantified toll of hundreds of thousands of conflict-related deaths a year across dozens of countries; overall fatalities eased slightly in 2025 but stayed higher than any other year since 2018, while the number of interstate conflicts doubled.
assessment.timeframe: Chronic and ongoing, with conflict-related fatalities near a multi-year high and interstate armed conflict rising sharply in 2025.

claims.text: The overall estimated number of conflict-related fatalities reduced slightly, by 4.2 per cent, from 249,000 in 2024 to 238,000 in 2025 — still higher than any other year in the period 2018-25 (SIPRI Yearbook 2026).

There were five major armed conflicts in 2025 (involving over 10,000 conflict-related fatalities each), one more than in 2024, while the number of high-intensity conflicts (1,000-9,999 fatalities) fell from 23 in 2024 to 20 in 2025 (SIPRI Yearbook 2026).

The number of interstate armed conflicts doubled from three in 2024 to six in 2025, involving at least 13 states, while the number of states with armed conflict on their territory fell slightly from 50 in 2024 to 49 in 2025 (SIPRI Yearbook 2026).

description: Ongoing state-based and civil wars that already kill hundreds of thousands annually and displace tens of millions more, with conflict-related fatalities holding near their highest annual level in years and interstate conflict doubling in 2025. Escalation, spillover between neighboring conflicts, and breakdown of humanitarian norms are the primary pathways to wider regional or global instability.
name: Global Armed Conflict
